newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to compensate 3 bln litas of savings.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to compensate 3 bln litas of savings.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that a government plan to compensate bank depositors whose savings were devoured by hyper-inflation in 1990-91 will cost 3.08 billion litas.
"The plan will cost 3.08 billion litas...We will need to compensate 1.1 million inhabitants for 1.4 million accounts," Vagnorius said at a news conference.

Vagnorius said the plan would be paid for by the sale of state assets, which will be transfered to a special property and savings restoration fund. "All the state-run property and its management will gradually be passed to this fund," he said.
"In the future, the state will not own the companies or the shares in the companies," he said.
"We want the ministries to be political institutions and not direct managers of companies," he said.
Vagnorius said the fund's functions would be to compensate depositors who held bank accounts before February 26, 1991, to manage state property and to pepare it for privatisation.
Vagnorius told Reuters that compensation will be paid over a period of five years.
The draft law which will be sent to parliament says pensioners will be the first group of people compensated and 6,000 litas will be the maximum amount paid to any one depositor from the fund.
